_note: Everyday Phrasebook — the function bank behind the in-session phrase help, the pre-start scene card and the 'Say It: Everyday' drill. Organised by conversational function, not place: these are the small moves that keep a real conversation moving when vocabulary, speed or social pressure gets in the way. Scene-specific lines may also appear as `key_expressions` in survival_situations.json / cases/lounge/*.json.

_phrase_schema.function: what this sentence DOES, shown alone at reveal level 1 so the learner tries their own English first
_phrase_schema.gloss: native-language note, keyed by language code; `en` is the fallback
_phrase_schema.register: casual | neutral | polite — everyday English fails on register far more often than on grammar
_phrase_schema.why: one line on when this works and when it does not
_phrase_schema.skeleton: optional hand-written level-2 frame with ___ blanks; derived from `en` when omitted
_phrase_schema.keywords: words that count as having used this, for the live 'you said it' tick

categories.name: When you didn't catch it
categories.goal: Keep the conversation alive instead of nodding at something you did not understand.

phrases.en: Sorry, could you say that again?

gloss.en: Ask them to repeat the whole thing
gloss.ko: 다시 한 번 말해 달라고 부탁하기

phrases.why: Works with anyone — a stranger, a professor, a friend. Safer than "What?", which can sound blunt.

phrases.en: Sorry, did you say Tuesday?
phrases.function: Check the one word you missed

gloss.en: Repeat back just the part you are unsure about

phrases.why: It shows you followed the rest and protects the details that matter: times, names and numbers.

phrases.en: Sorry, what does that mean?

gloss.en: Ask about a word you heard but do not know

phrases.why: Not knowing a word is normal; asking is faster and safer than guessing.

phrases.en: Could you slow down a little? I'm still learning.

gloss.en: Ask for a slower pace and give a reason
gloss.ko: 조금 천천히 말해 달라고 이유와 함께 부탁하기

phrases.why: Giving the reason helps people slow down for more than one sentence.

phrases.en: Could you spell that for me?
phrases.function: Check the spelling of a name or place

gloss.en: Ask someone to spell an important word

phrases.why: Essential for names, email addresses and locations — details you cannot safely guess from sound.

phrases.en: Could you write that down for me?
phrases.function: Ask to have important information written down

gloss.en: Ask for a written version of a detail

phrases.why: A practical rescue for an address, phone number, platform, room number or unfamiliar name.

categories.name: When you need a moment
categories.goal: Hold your turn while you think, instead of going silent and losing it.

phrases.en: Let me think for a second.

gloss.en: Say out loud that you are thinking

phrases.why: Four words keep the turn yours; silence often invites the other person to jump in.

phrases.en: That's a good question — how do I put this?
phrases.function: Fill the gap while you search for words

gloss.en: Use a natural filler while you find the words
gloss.ko: 단어를 찾는 동안 자연스럽게 시간 벌기

phrases.why: It sounds thoughtful rather than stuck, and buys you a few calm seconds.

phrases.en: How do you say it in English — the thing you keep money in?
phrases.function: Describe a word you don't know

gloss.en: Describe the thing instead of stopping at the missing word

phrases.why: A high-value rescue skill: the conversation continues and the word is often handed to you.
phrases.skeleton: How do you say it in English — ___?

phrases.en: Sorry, I lost my train of thought. Where was I?

gloss.en: Admit you lost track and get back in
gloss.ko: 말의 흐름을 놓쳤을 때 자연스럽게 다시 이어가기

phrases.why: It is more natural than trailing off, and it lets the other person help you continue.

categories.name: When you need something
categories.goal: Make a clear, considerate request instead of a vague hint or a bare command.

phrases.en: Could you help me with ___?

gloss.en: Politely ask someone to help with a specific thing

phrases.why: The most reusable request frame: add the task, not a long explanation.

phrases.en: Would you mind ___?

gloss.en: Make a polite request for an action

phrases.why: Useful when the action affects you directly: opening a window, moving over, speaking up.

phrases.en: Is it okay if I ___?

gloss.en: Check before you do something
gloss.ko: 어떤 행동을 하기 전에 허락 구하기

phrases.why: Short, natural and useful in shared spaces, at work, and with new people.

categories.name: At a counter or restaurant
categories.goal: Handle the compact American phrases used when ordering, taking food away and paying.

phrases.en: Can I get ___?
phrases.function: Order or ask for an item

gloss.en: The natural US counter-service way to ask for something

phrases.why: In the U.S., this is the everyday ordering frame at cafés, delis and many stores — not a demand.

phrases.en: Could I get this to go?

gloss.en: Ask for takeaway food

phrases.why: "To go" is the everyday U.S. expression; it covers a drink, a new order or leftovers.

phrases.en: Could we split the check?
phrases.function: Ask to divide a restaurant bill

gloss.en: Ask to pay separately at a restaurant
gloss.ko: 식당 계산을 나눠서 할 수 있는지 묻기

phrases.why: "Check" is the usual U.S. restaurant word; ask before payment when separate cards are involved.

phrases.en: Is gratuity included?
phrases.function: Check whether a tip has already been added

gloss.en: Ask if the service charge or tip is already on the bill
gloss.ko: 팁 또는 서비스료가 이미 포함됐는지 확인하기

phrases.why: Especially useful for groups and visitors: it prevents accidentally tipping twice.

categories.name: When you need to find something
categories.goal: Get the exact location or service information you need without relying on gestures.

phrases.en: Could you tell me how to get to ___?

gloss.en: Ask how to reach a place

phrases.why: Works for a building, platform, office or neighborhood — not just tourist directions.
phrases.skeleton: Could you tell me how to get to ___?

phrases.en: Is this the right place for ___?
phrases.function: Check that you are in the right place

gloss.en: Confirm a location before waiting or lining up

phrases.why: A quick check prevents a very common real-life mistake: waiting in the wrong line or room.
phrases.skeleton: Is this the right place for ___?

phrases.en: Could you point me to the ___?

gloss.en: Ask someone to indicate a nearby place

phrases.why: Best for nearby essentials such as the restroom, exit, elevator or information desk.
phrases.skeleton: Could you point me to the ___?

categories.name: When you make or change plans
categories.goal: Set up a plan clearly, then repair it politely when real life changes.

phrases.en: What time works for you?

gloss.en: Let the other person suggest a time

phrases.why: More cooperative than naming one time and hoping it works.

phrases.en: Just to make sure, we're meeting at ___, right?

gloss.en: Repeat the key detail to make sure you understood

phrases.why: A tiny confirmation prevents missed meetings, wrong locations and timezone mistakes.
phrases.skeleton: Just to make sure, we're meeting at ___, right?

phrases.en: Something came up. Could we reschedule?

gloss.en: Politely ask to move an arrangement
gloss.ko: 약속을 변경할 수 있는지 정중하게 묻기

phrases.why: It gives a brief reason without oversharing and keeps the relationship warm.

categories.name: At an appointment or pickup desk
categories.goal: Check in, collect something and complete the first step at an unfamiliar desk without a long explanation.

phrases.en: I have an appointment under ___.

gloss.en: Give the name used for a booking

phrases.why: "Under [name]" is the compact phrase staff expect at clinics, salons, offices and reservations.

phrases.en: I'm here to pick up ___.

gloss.en: Tell the desk or counter why you are there

phrases.why: Works for an online order, prescription, package, document or food order.

phrases.en: Do I need to fill this out?
phrases.function: Ask whether a form is required

gloss.en: Check if you need to complete a form

phrases.why: Useful at reception desks, government offices, schools and services where the process is not obvious.

categories.name: On a bus or train
categories.goal: Confirm the route, the line and your stop before a transit mistake becomes expensive or stressful.

phrases.en: Does this bus go to ___?

gloss.en: Ask whether this vehicle goes to your destination

phrases.why: Ask before boarding when the route name or display is unclear; replace "bus" with "train" when needed.

phrases.en: Where should I get off for ___?

gloss.en: Ask where to leave the bus or train

phrases.why: More useful than asking only for a station name when you are headed to a building or landmark.
phrases.skeleton: Where should I get off for ___?

phrases.en: Is this the line for ___?

gloss.en: Confirm that you are waiting in the right line

phrases.why: Useful at buses, airport shuttles, ticket counters and any fast-moving queue.

categories.name: When you want to keep talking
categories.goal: Show interest and return the conversational ball instead of ending every answer with a full stop.

phrases.en: What have you been up to lately?

gloss.en: Invite someone to talk about their recent life

phrases.why: A warm, open question for friends, classmates and coworkers you already know a little.

phrases.en: How did that go?
phrases.function: Follow up on something they mentioned

gloss.en: Ask about the outcome of an event or plan
gloss.ko: 상대가 전에 말한 일의 결과를 물어보기

phrases.why: Remembering one detail makes a conversation feel attentive, not scripted.

phrases.en: What about you?

gloss.en: Invite the other person to share too

phrases.why: A tiny phrase with a large effect: it turns an answer into a two-way conversation.

categories.name: When you respond with care
categories.goal: Acknowledge the other person before you agree, disagree or move on.

phrases.en: That sounds tough.

gloss.en: Acknowledge that something sounds difficult

phrases.why: A simple, natural response when someone shares a problem; do not rush straight into advice.

phrases.en: That makes sense.

gloss.en: Acknowledge that their explanation is reasonable

phrases.why: Useful before a follow-up question or a different opinion, because it keeps the tone cooperative.

phrases.en: I see what you mean, but ___.

gloss.en: Recognise their point before giving your different view
gloss.ko: 상대의 의견을 인정한 뒤 부드럽게 다른 의견 말하기

phrases.why: The most useful soft-disagreement frame for work, study and everyday decisions.
phrases.skeleton: I see what you mean, but ___.

categories.name: When you need to say no or leave
categories.goal: Protect your time or preference without sounding cold, apologetic for too long, or trapped.

phrases.en: I'd love to, but I can't make it.

gloss.en: Say no while showing you appreciate the invitation

phrases.why: Warm and complete — you do not need to invent a detailed excuse.

phrases.en: Thanks for asking, but I'll pass this time.

gloss.en: Decline an offer without closing the relationship
gloss.ko: 제안은 고맙게 받고 이번에는 정중히 사양하기

phrases.why: Clearer than a hesitant maybe, especially when you do not want to explain why.

phrases.en: I should get going, but it was great talking to you.

gloss.en: Signal that you are leaving while ending on a positive note
gloss.ko: 대화를 긍정적인 분위기로 마무리하고 자리 뜨기

phrases.why: A graceful exit when you need to leave but do not want to seem abrupt.

categories.name: When you need to correct yourself
categories.goal: Fix a wrong word or unclear idea quickly, without apologising so much that the conversation stalls.

phrases.en: Sorry, I mean ___.

gloss.en: Replace the word or detail you just got wrong
gloss.ko: 방금 잘못 말한 단어나 정보를 바로 고치기

phrases.why: Use it immediately for names, dates, directions and small vocabulary mistakes.

phrases.en: What I meant was ___.

gloss.en: Restate an idea more clearly
gloss.ko: 의도한 뜻을 더 분명하게 다시 말하기

phrases.why: Better than repeating the same unclear sentence louder or more slowly.

phrases.en: Let me say that another way.

gloss.en: Start over with clearer wording
gloss.ko: 문장 전체를 더 분명하게 바꿔 말하기

phrases.why: Useful when the problem is not one word but the whole sentence or tone.
